title: The most unlikely Bundesliga winners of all - DW News
content: But 22 years ago, they shot up from the second tier to win the Bundesliga at the first go, crushing Bayern Munich on the way. If Otto Rehhagel hoped to carry some of the momentum from his team's march to the 1996-97 Bundesliga 2 title in to a daunting season in Germany's top flight, he was dealt an early blow when the fixture list came out. His revenge was first swift — as an 80th-minute goal from Michael Schjonberg secured the newly-promoted side a shock win on the opening day — then deep, with Kaiserslautern briefly breaking Bayern and Borussia Dortmund's decade-long duopoly with a title win forged on that first day. The side from a town with a population of less than 100,000 in the south-west of Germany drew an average gate of 36,709 to the Fritz Walter stadium in their victorious 2.Bundesliga campaign, with the name of their ground a nod to their rich history —Walter was captain of the West Germany side that pulled off one of the biggest shocks in World Cup history in 1954.

The 2. Bundesliga has been Germany’s second division since 1974, and over the past fifty years it’s become the stage where historic clubs rebuild and ambitious newcomers fight for promotion. In the early years, the league was split into North and South groups before being unified in 1981, and big names like Borussia Dortmund and Schalke 04 spent time here before returning to the Bundesliga. After reunification in the 1990s, East German clubs such as Hansa Rostock and Dynamo Dresden joined, adding new rivalries and flavor to the competition.

Through the 2000s and 2010s, the league earned its reputation as one of the most unpredictable in Europe. Clubs like Köln, Hertha BSC, and Stuttgart bounced back and forth between divisions, while SC Freiburg and Nürnberg enjoyed memorable title runs. Union Berlin’s steady rise eventually led to their breakthrough into the Bundesliga in 2019, showing how persistence in the 2. Bundesliga could pay off.

In recent years, the drama has only intensified. Schalke 04, Bochum, Arminia Bielefeld, and St. Pauli have all lifted titles, while Köln stands out historically with five championships—the most of any club. By 2025, more than 120 different teams had competed in the league, proving its role as a dynamic proving ground. Across five decades, the 2. Bundesliga has remained a place where fallen giants regroup, underdogs rise, and fans witness some of the most thrilling promotion battles in German football.
